newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate under pressure from auction.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate under pressure from auction.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates stood unchanged at 19.00 percent in early trade on Wednesday, but were nonetheless under pressure from a weak peso following a sharp drop in primary rates.
Dealers added that Tuesday's closing rate was higher than average trading levels for that session, thus although unchanged from the prior close, overnight Cetes were trading at a higher rates.
"The market is calm but under a little pressure from the sharp drop in Cetes rates," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes at Tuesday night's auction of government securities, their lowest level since a financial crisis triggered by a shock devaluation in December 1994.
"Primary rates fell substantially, which is prompting demand for dollars, and that in turn means dealers are gatting out of local debt," a money market analyst said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 2.3 centavos softer in early trade at 7.9200/7.9230 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper were down 10 percent at 19.50 percent.
Dealers said they expected overnight Cetes to trade at slightly more than 19 percent.
Liquidity of 294 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
